claim: The red fire ant Solenopsis invicta includes single-queen and multiple-queen colonies, which differ in behavior, physiology and ecology.
source: This species includes single-queen and multiple-queen colonies, which differ in behavior, physiology and ecology.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript describing the social polymorphism in fire ants.

claim: Social polymorphism in Solenopsis invicta is controlled by a pair of 'social chromosomes', SB and Sb, that carry distinct supergene variants.
source: This social polymorphism is controlled by a pair of 'social chromosomes', SB and Sb, that carry distinct supergene variants (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013.

claim: In single-queen colonies, workers and queens are SB/SB homozygotes.
source: In single-queen colonies, workers and queens are SB/SB homozygotes.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the genotype of individuals in single-queen colonies.

claim: In multiple-queen colonies, egg-laying queens are SB/Sb heterozygotes.
source: In multiple-queen colonies, egg-laying queens are SB/Sb heterozygotes, but workers can either be homozygous or heterozygous.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the genotype of queens in multiple-queen colonies.

claim: Sb/Sb queens are rare and their offspring are unviable.
source: Sb/Sb queens are rare and their offspring are unviable (Gotzek and Ross, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gotzek and Ross, 2007.

claim: Recombination is severely repressed between SB and Sb because of at least three inversions.
source: Furthermore, because of at least three inversions (Stolle et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2018), recombination is severely repressed between SB and Sb (Wang et al., 2013; Pracana et al., 2017a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The fire ant supergene system could be as young as 175,000 generations.
source: Importantly, the fire ant supergene system could be as young as 175,000 generations.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the age of the supergene system.

claim: Sb has accumulated non-synonymous single nucleotide substitutions and repetitive elements.
source: Accordingly, Sb has accumulated non-synonymous single nucleotide substitutions and repetitive elements (Stolle et al., 2019; Pracana et al., 2017a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Stolle et al., 2019 and Pracana et al., 2017a.

claim: Gene content in SB and Sb is highly similar.
source: Despite Sb degeneration, gene content in SB and Sb is highly similar (Wang et al., 2013; Pracana et al., 2017a), likely because of the system's young age and purifying selection in haploid males (Hall and Goodisman, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2013 and Pracana et al., 2017a.

claim: 2877 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with one allele in all SB individuals and a different allele in all Sb individuals were identified, affecting 352 genes.
source: By comparing the two groups of males we identified 2877 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with one allele in all SB individuals and a different allele in all Sb individuals, affecting 352 genes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from genomic analysis.

claim: Among the 3.4% of SNPs affecting coding sequence, almost half changed the amino-acid sequence.
source: Among the 3.4% of SNPs affecting coding sequence, almost half changed the amino-acid sequence, with one change to a premature stop codon (47.7% non-synonymous vs. 52.3% synonymous changes).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from genomic analysis.

claim: Seven genes had consistent expression differences between variants across all populations.
source: We found that seven of the genes (5.7%) had consistent expression differences between variants across all populations (linear mixed-effects model; Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjusted p<0.05, Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis and Figure 1.

claim: The Sb variants of 'pheromone-binding protein Gp-9/OBP3' (LOC105194481), 'retinol-binding protein pinta-like' (LOC105199327) and uncharacterized LOC105193135 were consistently more highly expressed.
source: Expression bias went in both directions: the Sb variants of 'pheromone-binding protein Gp-9/OBP3' (LOC105194481), 'retinol-binding protein pinta-like' (LOC105199327) and uncharacterized LOC105193135 were consistently more highly expressed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: The SB variants of 'ejaculatory bulb-specific protein 3' (LOC105199531), 'carbohydrate sulfotransferase 11-like' (LOC105193134), 'calcium-independent phospholipase A2-gamma' (LOC105203065) and uncharacterized LOC105199756 were consistently more highly expressed.
source: In contrast, the SB variants of 'ejaculatory bulb-specific protein 3' (LOC105199531), 'carbohydrate sulfotransferase 11-like' (LOC105193134), 'calcium-independent phospholipase A2-gamma' (LOC105203065) and uncharacterized LOC105199756 were consistently more highly expressed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: No effect of body part or caste on allelic expression was found for any gene in the supergene region.
source: We found no effect of body part or caste on allelic expression for any gene in the supergene region (DESeq2's Logarithmic Ratio Test and all pairwise Wald comparisons between interaction terms; all BH adjusted p>0.05).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from statistical analysis.

claim: Correlation of allelic bias was stronger between invasive populations (Spearman's r2 = 0.67) than between either invasive and the native population (Spearman's r2 = 0.21 and 0.18).
source: Our findings were in line with our expectation: correlation was stronger between invasive populations (Spearman's r2 = 0.67), than between either invasive and the native population (Spearman's r2 = 0.21 and 0.18).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from correlation analysis.

claim: Population ancestry has a stronger effect on allelic expression bias than geographic proximity.
source: This result was further supported by a linear mixed-effects model of all data: population ancestry has a stronger effect on allelic expression bias than geographic proximity (respective interaction terms with the effect of gene: F = 3.42, p<10−15 and F = 0.94, p=0.65).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from statistical analysis.

claim: Socially biased genes were overrepresented in the supergene region.
source: Such genes were indeed overrepresented in the supergene region (Figure 2a, 33 out of 474, 12 expected by chance, χ2 = 29.7, p<10−7).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis and Figure 2a.

claim: Most socially biased genes had higher expression in multiple-queen colonies than in single-queen colonies (274 out of 293, i.e., 94%).
source: Next, we examined the direction of expression bias: we found that most socially biased genes had higher expression in multiple-queen colonies than in single-queen colonies (274 out of 293, i.e., 94%; binomial test, p<10−15).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with statistical support.

claim: The pattern of higher expression in multiple-queen colonies was not specific to the supergene.
source: However, this pattern was not specific to the supergene (χ2=1.04, p=0.3, Figure 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis and Figure 2b.

claim: A model allowing for gene-specific dosage compensation fits the data better than a null model.
source: The second model (red line), additionally allows for the effect of gene-specific dosage compensation by increasing expression of B-alleles in SB/Sb individuals in multiple queen-colonies. This model fits the data much better and it is significantly different from the null model (analysis of variance p<10−5).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from model comparison.

claim: Fifteen genes showed allelic bias but no differences in gene expression between social forms.
source: However, fifteen of the 294 genes showed allelic bias but no differences in gene expression between social forms (5%; Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with reference to Figure 4c.

claim: Most genes with allelic bias but no social bias (12 out of 15) had higher expression in SB.
source: Most of these genes (12) had higher expression in SB, with only three being more highly expressed in Sb (binomial test, p=0.03).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with statistical support.

claim: The median expression of SB alleles of these 15 genes was 5.9-fold higher than that of Sb alleles.
source: In line with this result, the median expression of SB alleles of these 15 genes was 5.9-fold higher than that of Sb alleles (Wilcoxon signed rank test p=0.0008 against equal expression).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with statistical support.

claim: As the number of non-synonymous mutations increases, the allelic bias towards SB increases.
source: Indeed, as the number of non-synonymous mutations increases, so does the allelic bias towards SB (coefficient = 0.052, p=0.01).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from regression analysis.

claim: Eight genes had both allele-biased and socially-biased expression.
source: From the 294 genes analyzed in the previous section, eight (3%) had both allele-biased and socially-biased expression (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with reference to Figure 4d.

claim: Five out of 8 Sb biased genes were significantly more highly expressed in multiple-queen colonies.
source: Their expression patterns were strongly directionally biased towards higher expression in Sb and in multiple-queen colonies (5 out 8 Sb biased genes were significantly more highly expressed in multiple-queen colonies Figure 4d; compared to 1 out of 15 for SB biased genes, χ2 = 5.8, p=0.02; Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with statistical support and reference to Figure 4d and 4c.

claim: Only 3 of the seven genes with consistent allelic bias in all populations were also differentially expressed between social forms.
source: Consistent with the lack of direct correlation between allelic bias and social bias, only 3 of the seven genes with consistent allelic bias in all populations were also differentially expressed between social forms (Supplementary file 2): 'pheromone-binding protein Gp-9' (LOC105194481), 'ejaculatory bulb-specific protein 3' (LOC105199531) and 'retinol-binding protein pinta-like' (LOC105199327).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: Suppressed recombination reduces the efficacy of purifying selection through Hill-Robertson interference, which can lead to gene degeneration.
source: Suppressed recombination reduces the efficacy of purifying selection through Hill-Robertson interference, which can lead to gene degeneration (Charlesworth, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Charlesworth, 2016.

claim: Evolutionary antagonism can emerge when selection favors multiple phenotypic optima within a population.
source: Evolutionary antagonism can emerge when selection favors multiple phenotypic optima within a population.
evidence: This is a direct statement about evolutionary theory.

claim: Supergenes controlling ecologically important traits are widespread.
source: We now know that supergenes controlling ecologically important traits are widespread. Examples include flower heterostyly in Primula (Li et al., 2016), mating type in Mycrobotryum fungi (Branco et al., 2018), Batesian mimicry in butterflies (Joron et al., 2011; Kunte et al., 2014), mating behavior in white-throated sparrows (Zinzow-Kramer et al., 2015; Tuttle et al., 2016) and male sexual morphs in ruff sandpipers (Küpper et al., 2016; Lamichhaney et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on different supergene systems.

claim: The non-recombining portions of sex chromosomes are extensively studied examples of supergenes.
source: The non-recombining portions of sex chromosomes are extensively studied examples of supergenes (Bergero and Charlesworth, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bergero and Charlesworth, 2009.

claim: Studies focusing on young sex chromosome systems suggest that sex chromosome evolution could be driven mostly by processes resulting from suppressed recombination rather than by antagonistic selection.
source: However, studies focusing on young sex chromosome systems suggest otherwise (Dufresnes et al., 2015; Nozawa et al., 2014; Alekseyenko et al., 2013; Muyle et al., 2012; Charlesworth et al., 2005; Stöck et al., 2011). Indeed, sex chromosome evolution could be driven mostly by processes resulting from suppressed recombination rather than by antagonistic selection (Branco et al., 2018; Cavoto et al., 2018; Branco et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on young sex chromosome systems.

claim: The social supergene of the red fire ant Solenopsis invicta is an excellent model for comparing how evolutionary antagonism and the consequences of suppressed recombination shape early supergene evolution.
source: The social supergene of the red fire ant Solenopsis invicta is an excellent model for comparing how evolutionary antagonism and the consequences of suppressed recombination shape early supergene evolution.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the suitability of the fire ant system as a model.

claim: The fire ant supergene offers a rare glimpse into the evolutionary forces shaping the early stages of supergene evolution.
source: It thus offers a rare glimpse into the evolutionary forces shaping the early stages of supergene evolution (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the value of the fire ant system with a citation.

claim: Modifications in the genomic sequence can lead to gene expression changes.
source: Modifications in the genomic sequence can lead to gene expression changes (Denver et al., 2005; Rifkin et al., 2005), the accumulation of mutations in Sb alleles of some genes could therefore result in SB/Sb expression bias.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Denver et al., 2005 and Rifkin et al., 2005.

claim: If mutations go to fixation because of inefficient purifying selection, they would likely result in consistent allelic bias across all tissues.
source: For instance, if such mutations go to fixation because of inefficient purifying selection, they would likely result in consistent allelic bias across all tissues.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the expected pattern of expression.

claim: If mutations go to fixation because they are adaptive responses to antagonistic selection, their expression levels would be likely to require tissue-specific fine-tuning for particular functions.
source: Alternatively, if such mutations go to fixation because they are adaptive responses to antagonistic selection, their expression levels would be likely to require tissue-specific fine-tuning for particular functions. This process should result in tissue-specific allelic bias, as observed across human tissues (GTEx Consortium, 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the expected pattern of expression with a citation to human tissue data.

claim: The accumulation of deleterious mutations in Sb alleles should lead to lower expression levels due to impacts in regulatory sequences.
source: The accumulation of deleterious mutations in Sb alleles should lead to lower expression levels due to impacts in regulatory sequences.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the expected effect of deleterious mutations.

claim: Selection against the expression of deleterious alleles should result in the downregulation of some Sb alleles.
source: Additionally, selection against the expression of deleterious alleles should result in the downregulation of some Sb alleles (Ma et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2019; Pucholt et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis with citations to supporting studies.

claim: If lower Sb expression occurs for dosage-sensitive genes, selection should favor upregulation of the corresponding SB alleles.
source: If lower Sb expression occurs for dosage-sensitive genes, selection should favor upregulation of the corresponding SB alleles.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about dosage compensation.

claim: In male Drosophila melanogaster the entire X chromosome is expressed at roughly twice the level of autosomes to compensate for the lack of expression in the highly degenerated Y chromosome.
source: For instance, in male Drosophila melanogaster the entire X chromosome is expressed at roughly twice the level of autosomes to compensate for the lack of expression in the highly degenerated Y chromosome (Conrad and Akhtar, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Conrad and Akhtar, 2012.

claim: In Drosophila miranda, dosage compensation occurs only at a gene-by-gene level.
source: In species with much younger sex chromosomes such as Drosophila miranda, dosage compensation instead occurs only at a gene-by-gene level (Alekseyenko et al., 2013; Nozawa et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Alekseyenko et al., 2013 and Nozawa et al., 2018.

claim: Because the fire ant supergene is young, individual genes for which the Sb allele has begun to degenerate would show evidence of dosage compensation.
source: Because the fire ant supergene is young, we hypothesize that individual genes for which the Sb allele has begun to degenerate would show evidence of dosage compensation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about dosage compensation in the fire ant.

claim: For genes with dosage compensation, the SB allele would be more highly expressed than the Sb allele, while their combined total expression should be similar between SB/Sb and SB/SB individuals.
source: For such genes, the SB allele would be more highly expressed than the Sb allele, while their combined total expression should be similar between SB/Sb and SB/SB individuals.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the expected pattern of expression with dosage compensation.

claim: The supergene region is expected to be enriched for genes with alleles that are beneficial for one of the social forms but detrimental for the other.
source: We thus expect that the supergene region is enriched for genes with alleles that are beneficial for one of the social forms but detrimental for the other (Zemp et al., 2016; Vicoso et al., 2013; Khil et al., 2004; Parsch and Ellegren, 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis with citations to supporting studies.

claim: Genes with antagonistic alleles are more likely to also show differences in expression between social forms, resulting in an enrichment of socially biased expression in the supergene.
source: Genes with such alleles are more likely to also show differences in expression between social forms, resulting in an enrichment of socially biased expression in the supergene.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the expected pattern of expression.

claim: Increased expression of Sb alleles is more likely to result from adaptation than from gene degeneration.
source: In contrast, increased expression of Sb alleles is more likely to result from adaptation (Harrison et al., 2012; Pál et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis with citations to supporting studies.

claim: Given the expected general pattern of Sb downregulation due to degeneration, genes with high expression of the Sb allele are more likely to be adaptive.
source: Following this logic and given the expected general pattern of Sb downregulation due to degeneration, genes with high expression of the Sb allele are more likely to be adaptive.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the interpretation of Sb expression patterns.

claim: Because Sb should be enriched in alleles beneficial for multiple-queen colonies, genes with high expression in multiple-queen colonies will tend to show Sb bias.
source: Furthermore, because Sb should be enriched in alleles beneficial for multiple-queen colonies, we expect that genes with high expression in multiple-queen colonies will tend to show Sb bias.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a hypothesis about the expected pattern of expression.

claim: Most genes in the social chromosome show no strong allelic bias.
source: We find that most genes in the social chromosome show no strong allelic bias and that there is no clear pattern of supergene-wide expression bias towards either variant.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: There is no clear pattern of supergene-wide expression bias towards either variant.
source: We find that most genes in the social chromosome show no strong allelic bias and that there is no clear pattern of supergene-wide expression bias towards either variant.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: Genes with biased expression tend to show patterns consistent with gene degeneration, such as lower Sb expression with increasing numbers of non-synonymous mutations.
source: Genes with biased expression tend to show patterns consistent with gene degeneration, such as lower Sb expression with increasing numbers of non-synonymous mutations.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: More genes are SB biased than expected given differences in expression between social forms, a pattern consistent with partial dosage compensation.
source: Additionally, we find that more genes are SB biased than expected given differences in expression between social forms, a pattern consistent with partial dosage compensation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: The accumulation of non-synonymous mutations in Sb alleles correlates with an allelic bias towards SB, consistent with ongoing Sb degeneration.
source: Accordingly, the accumulation of non-synonymous mutations in Sb alleles correlates with an allelic bias towards SB, consistent with ongoing Sb degeneration.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: There is an overrepresentation of Sb-biased genes among genes with higher expression in individuals from multiple-queen colonies.
source: Despite these observations, we find an overrepresentation of Sb-biased genes among genes with higher expression in individuals from multiple-queen colonies.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: The overrepresentation of Sb-biased genes among genes with higher expression in multiple-queen colonies indicates that antagonistic selection has shaped the expression patterns in the fire ant supergene.
source: This result indicates that antagonistic selection has also shaped the expression patterns in the fire ant supergene.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: 252 additional SNPs with fixed differences between SB and Sb individuals were found in South America.
source: We found 252 additional SNPs with fixed differences between SB and Sb individuals in South America, and 23,022 additional fixed differences between SB and Sb in North America.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from genomic analysis.

claim: 23,022 additional fixed differences between SB and Sb were found in North America.
source: We found 252 additional SNPs with fixed differences between SB and Sb individuals in South America, and 23,022 additional fixed differences between SB and Sb in North America.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from genomic analysis.

claim: The number of fixed differences in North America is 4-fold higher than expected due to differences in sampling size alone.
source: The latter number is 4-fold higher than expected due to differences in sampling size alone and is in line with lower genetic diversity of both supergene variants in North America due to the invasion bottleneck.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from genomic analysis.

claim: The high number of fixed differences in North America is in line with lower genetic diversity of both supergene variants in North America due to the invasion bottleneck.
source: The latter number is 4-fold higher than expected due to differences in sampling size alone and is in line with lower genetic diversity of both supergene variants in North America due to the invasion bottleneck.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Among the 352 genes with fixed differences between SB and Sb, 122 had sufficient expression for analysis of differences between alleles.
source: Among the 352 genes with fixed differences between SB and Sb in this combined dataset, 122 had sufficient expression for analysis of differences between alleles.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: The general lack of tissue-specific fine-tuning of allelic expression bias in the supergene suggests that most of this bias is due to the accumulation of neutral or deleterious mutations in Sb rather than being adaptive.
source: The general lack of tissue-specific fine-tuning of allelic expression bias in the supergene suggests that most of this bias is due to the accumulation of neutral or deleterious mutations (Stolle et al., 2019; Pracana et al., 2017a) in Sb rather than being adaptive.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings with citations.

claim: The effects of suppressed recombination on genomic architecture explain most of the allelic biases in the supergene region.
source: Together, these results support the idea that the effects of suppressed recombination on genomic architecture explain most of the allelic biases in the supergene region.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: There were 293 socially biased genes with known chromosomal locations.
source: There were 293 socially biased genes with known chromosomal locations (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: The trend of social bias is genome-wide and cannot be explained by Sb degeneration alone.
source: Since the trend of social bias is genome-wide, it cannot be explained by Sb degeneration alone.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The expression levels of SB and Sb are balanced for most genes without differences between social forms.
source: Instead, we find that the expression levels of SB and Sb are balanced for most genes without differences between social forms (black line in Figure 3, linear regression passes through the point 0.5, 0.5 with a non-significant deviation of 0.0058; p=0.32).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from statistical analysis with reference to Figure 3.

claim: At the extremes of the distribution, allelic bias is higher when social bias is higher.
source: At the extremes of the distribution, however, allelic bias is higher when social bias is higher.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: Higher SB allele expression in heterozygous individuals does not imply higher expression in single-queen colonies.
source: Thus, higher SB allele expression in heterozygous individuals does not imply higher expression in single-queen colonies.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Most genes had no significant allelic or socially biased expression (256, i.e., 87%).
source: Most genes had no significant allelic or socially biased expression (256, i.e., 87%; Figure 4a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The general and gene-specific patterns are hallmarks of dosage compensation.
source: The general and gene-specific patterns are hallmarks of dosage compensation: Lower expression of Sb alleles is compensated for by higher expression of SB alleles, resulting in the absence of expression differences between social forms.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The overall trends and gene-specific patterns both indicate that dosage compensation occurs in gene-specific manners rather than being a response to global Sb-inactivation.
source: Importantly, the overall trends and gene-specific patterns both indicate that this dosage compensation occurs in gene-specific manners rather than being a response to global Sb-inactivation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Coding-sequence degeneration could lead to lower expression.
source: This indicates that coding-sequence degeneration could lead to lower expression, or alternatively that some genes generally degenerate faster than others.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The enrichment of multiple-queen biased genes in the Sb variant is consistent with antagonistic selection.
source: This enrichment of multiple-queen biased genes in the Sb variant is consistent with antagonistic selection.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The fixation of non-synonymous mutations in Sb alleles correlates with lower expression levels.
source: We additionally showed that the fixation of non-synonymous mutations in Sb alleles correlates with lower expression levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: It is unlikely that the trend of enrichment in high multiple-queen expression among Sb biased genes would have arisen neutrally.
source: We therefore consider it unlikely that the trend of enrichment in high multiple-queen expression among Sb biased genes would have arisen neutrally.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Genes with Sb and multiple-queen bias were likely under antagonistic selection.
source: Given the patterns of ongoing degeneration in Sb, we conclude that genes with Sb and multiple-queen bias were likely under antagonistic selection.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The neo-Y chromosome of Drosophila miranda is enriched in male-biased genes in the gonads.
source: Similarly, the neo-Y chromosome of Drosophila miranda is enriched in male-biased genes in the gonads (Zhou and Bachtrog, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhou and Bachtrog, 2012.

claim: Three genes stood out as candidates for contributing to the social polymorphism because they were differentially expressed between social forms and had variant-specific allele expression in all populations.
source: In particular, three genes stood out because they were differentially expressed between social forms and had variant-specific allele expression in all populations.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: For 'Pheromone-binding protein Gp-9' (LOC105194481), the Sb allele was more highly expressed.
source: For the first gene, 'Pheromone-binding protein Gp-9' (LOC105194481), also known as OBP-3, the Sb allele was more highly expressed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: Five fixed differences between SB and Sb were found for 'Pheromone-binding protein Gp-9', four of which could affect protein efficiency.
source: We found five fixed differences between SB and Sb for this gene, four of which could affect protein efficiency (consistent with previous findings [Krieger and Ross, 2002]).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from genomic analysis with a citation.

claim: For 'Ejaculatory bulb-specific protein 3' (LOC105199531), the SB allele was more highly expressed.
source: For the second gene, 'Ejaculatory bulb-specific protein 3' (LOC105199531), which also contains an insect odorant binding protein domain (InterPro IPR005055), the SB allele was more highly expressed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from expression analysis.

claim: Orthologs of 'Ejaculatory bulb-specific protein 3' are associated with mating in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Orthologs of this gene are associated with mating (Laturney and Billeter, 2014) in Drosophila melanogaster, sexual behavior in a moth (Bohbot et al., 1998), subcaste differences in bumblebees (Wolschin et al., 2012), venom production in social hornets (Yoon et al., 2015) and caste differences in the termite Reticulitermes flavipes (Steller et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on orthologs.

claim: LOC105199327 is likely a Pinta retinol-binding protein.
source: Finally, LOC105199327 is likely a Pinta retinol-binding protein.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an inference about gene function.

claim: Retinol-binding proteins help pigment transport and vision in D. melanogaster and the butterfly Papilio xuthus.
source: Such proteins help pigment transport and vision in D. melanogaster and the butterfly Papilio xuthus (Pelosi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pelosi et al., 2018.

claim: All three candidate genes have putative functions related to environmental perception.
source: In sum, all three candidate genes have putative functions related to environmental perception, in line with the complex social phenotype requiring subtle changes in environmental perception or signaling (Favreau et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings with a citation.

claim: Genes with higher expression of the SB allele than the Sb allele tend to either lack expression differences between social forms or have lower expression in multiple-queen than in single-queen colonies.
source: In particular, genes with higher expression of the SB allele than the Sb allele tend to either lack expression differences between social forms or have lower expression in multiple-queen than in single-queen colonies.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: Both patterns of SB-biased expression are consistent with the idea that suppressed recombination leads to degeneration in Sb and thus lower Sb allele expression.
source: Both patterns are consistent with the idea that suppressed recombination leads to degeneration in Sb and thus lower Sb allele expression.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: In some cases, a dosage compensation mechanism through higher expression of the healthy SB allele leads to similar expression levels in both social forms.
source: In some cases, a dosage compensation mechanism through higher expression of the healthy SB allele leads to similar expression levels in both social forms.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: In cases where no dosage compensation occurs, overall expression is lower in multiple-queen colonies than in single-queen colonies.
source: In cases where no dosage compensation occurs, overall expression is lower in multiple-queen colonies than in single-queen colonies.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Genes with higher expression of the Sb allele than the SB allele are also biased towards higher expression in multiple-queen colonies, consistent with evolutionary antagonism favoring the accumulation of beneficial alleles for multiple-queen individuals in Sb.
source: Conversely, we also show that genes with higher expression of the Sb allele than the SB allele are also biased towards higher expression in multiple-queen colonies. This pattern is consistent with evolutionary antagonism favoring the accumulation of beneficial alleles for multiple-queen individuals in Sb, the supergene variant found only in this social form.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding and its interpretation.

claim: Multiple complex evolutionary forces can simultaneously act on a young supergene system.
